description: A program-prototype-name as the operand of CALL and CANCEL — §2023:14.9.4.2 Format 2's bracket-omitted spelling `CALL program-prototype-name-1` and §2023:14.9.5.2's third operand alternative — which §2023:8.4.6.8 scopes to 'the program-name of a containing program definition or a program-prototype-name declared in the REPOSITORY paragraph'. ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduced it (its clause 8.4.5.7 carries the same sentence); COBOL-85 has no program-prototype-names, and its CALL and CANCEL identifier-1 shall be a data item (§2023:14.9.4.3 SR1, §2023:14.9.5.3 SR1). The spelling is written exactly like identifier-1, so there is nothing for a recognition gate to see: below 2002 the word is ROUTED as identifier-1 (CallBinder.ProgramPrototypeNamesExist, a behavioral read, DESIGN-version-conformance-pipeline §1.1 item 3) and one that names no data item is the §2023:8.4.2.1 undefined reference, COBOL1639. The containing spelling needs no REPOSITORY entry, so this row's own witness is it: until kb/Work PB4509 an 85 compile ACCEPTED a nested program's `CALL OUTER` as a prototype CALL.
display: a program-prototype-name as the CALL / CANCEL operand
vcr: 2002 introduction (ISO/IEC 1989:2002 clause 8.4.5.7; Annex E covers 2014-2023 only)
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PPNC1.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    CALL "PPNC2".
    STOP RUN.
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PPNC2.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
P.
    CALL PPNC1.
    EXIT PROGRAM.
END PROGRAM PPNC2.
END PROGRAM PPNC1.
